text:
Juuse Saros stopped 40 of 42 shots, and the Predators turned that into a shootout win in Las Vegas, their seventh straight and the end of the Golden Knights' four-game run. Nashville was drafting Saros 99th overall back in 2013, out of HPK in Finland, and on a night when the game tilted the other way for long stretches, he is the reason it stayed close.

Our numbers say Vegas played the better game. Expected goals, which measure the quality of chances, favored the Golden Knights 3.71 to 3.26, and the Predators' goalie was credited with saving about 1.7 goals more than the shots he faced should have allowed. Vegas ran away with the first period, 1.64 to 0.81 in expected goals, and Victor Olofsson tied it at 1-1 after Ryan O'Reilly's opener. Rasmus Andersson put Vegas ahead in the second. Nashville pushed back in the third, and O'Reilly tied it with his second goal, a wrist shot we gave only a 7% chance of going in. In a replay of every shot, Vegas wins this game 57% of the time.

Nobody scored in the first round of the shootout. Trevor Connelly beat Saros's counterpart Adin Hill's opposite number early, but Filip Forsberg and Roman Josi both scored for Nashville, and Josi's goal ended it after Jack Eichel was stopped. Nashville carries its seven-game winning streak out of Vegas, though the Golden Knights had beaten them 5-2 in October. Vegas drops to 4-0 over its last four... no: its four-game winning streak is over, and it will look back on a night when it out-chanced the opponent and still left with one point.
